Welcome
Sophia Koiston Headteacher
It is a privilege to welcome you to Sidlesham Primary School. My name is Mrs Koiston and I am the very proud Headteacher of our wonderful village school — a place where big ambitions grow in a small, nurturing community. At Sidlesham, our purpose is clear: to secure the very best life chances for every child through an inspiring, high-quality education. Everything we do is driven by this commitment.

Clubs
At Sidlesham Primary School, we offer a wide range of clubs and enrichment opportunities to help children develop new skills, interests and friendships.
We believe that learning goes beyond the classroom, and we are proud to provide opportunities for all pupils to take part in activities that build confidence, teamwork and enjoyment.
What We Offer
Our clubs vary throughout the year and may include:
sports clubs and competitions
music and performing arts
outdoor learning and bushcraft
lunchtime and after-school clubs
We aim to ensure that there is something for everyone.
Why it Matters
Clubs and enrichment activities help pupils to:
develop confidence and independence
build friendships across year groups
discover new interests and talents
stay active and engaged
We encourage all pupils to take part wherever possible.
Current Clubs
You can find full details of our current clubs, including times and how to sign up, in the document below:

Wraparound Care
At Sidlesham Primary School, we offer a range of wraparound care options to support families before and after the school day.
Our provision provides a safe, welcoming and flexible environment where children can relax, play and socialise.
Opening Times
We offer wraparound care throughout the week:
Morning provision (Hummingbirds): from 7:30am
After school provision (Hummingbirds): until 5:30pm, Monday to Thursday
After school provision (Active8 Minds): until 5:30pm on Fridays (Ofsted registration number: 2802645)
This ensures families have access to childcare across the full school week.
What to Expect
Our wraparound care provides a calm and friendly environment where children can:
relax before or after the school day
play and socialise with friends
take part in a range of activities
enjoy a safe and supervised setting
We aim to create a positive and nurturing experience for all children.
Providers
Hummingbirds – our in-school provision, led by school staff
Active8 Minds – external provider offering Friday after-school care (Ofsted registration number: 2802645)
Both provisions work closely with the school to ensure consistency and high standards of care.

Bookings and Enquiries
To find out more, please contact the school office:
📧 office@sidleshamprimaryschool.co.uk
Booking is made via the MCAS parent app for Hummingbirds and directly with Active8 Minds for Friday afternoon sessions.
We are happy to help with any questions or specific requirements.

Starting school in September 2027?
Choosing your child's first school is a big decision, and we'd love you to come and see Sidlesham for yourself.
We are a small, ambitious village school where children are known well, supported to thrive and encouraged to grow in ambition, confidence and kindness.
Reception 2027 Open Mornings
Wednesday 16th September Thursday 24th September Friday 2nd October Wednesday 14th October Wednesday 11th November 9:00–10:30am
Can't make one of these dates? We'd still love to meet you. Contact our school office and we'll arrange another opportunity for you to visit.
Come and see Sidlesham in action
Meet our Reception team, explore our Early Years environment and discover what makes our small school special - from a nurturing start and strong foundations in reading and maths to outdoor learning, sport, music and wider opportunities.
Why Sidlesham?
Known well - As a small school, relationships matter. Children are known as individuals and families quickly become part of our school community.
A strong start - Our Reception provision combines a nurturing Early Years environment with strong foundations in communication, reading, phonics and mathematics.
Learning beyond the classroom - Our rural setting and extensive grounds give children opportunities to learn outdoors alongside sport, music, creativity, clubs and wider experiences.
Growing together - Our vision is for children to grow in ambition, confidence and kindness, developing the knowledge, independence and character they need for the future.
Applying for a Place
Admissions to Sidlesham Primary School are managed by West Sussex County Council.
To apply for a school place, please visit:
West Sussex School Admissions
The deadline for applications for September 2027 is 15 January 2027.
Visit Us
We warmly welcome visits to our school so you can see our learning environment and meet our staff and pupils.
Please contact the school office to arrange a visit:📞 01243 641 238📧 office@sidleshamprimaryschool.co.uk
Starting School
We understand that starting school is an important milestone for both children and families.
We work closely with parents and carers to ensure a smooth and positive transition into school. This includes visits, transition sessions and opportunities for your child to become familiar with their new environment.

Personal Development
At Sidlesham Primary School, our Personal Development Curriculum helps children develop the knowledge, understanding and behaviours they need to build positive relationships, look after their health and wellbeing, stay safe, participate responsibly in an increasingly digital world and contribute positively to their community.
Our curriculum reflects our school vision:
Growing Together in Ambition, Confidence and Kindness
and our school rules:
Ready • Respectful • Safe
It includes statutory Relationships Education and Health Education, relevant National Curriculum Science, and wider Personal Development learning that prepares pupils for the opportunities, responsibilities and experiences of later life.
Our Personal Development Curriculum
Our curriculum is organised through six interconnected strands:
These strands provide a coherent and progressive curriculum from EYFS to Year 6. Important concepts are introduced, revisited and developed with increasing sophistication as children move through the school.
How the Curriculum is Organised
EYFS has its own age-appropriate enquiry within each strand.
Years 1–3 follow a three-year Cycle A/B/C, while Years 4–6 follow a separate three-year Cycle A/B/C. This structure reflects our mixed-age classes while ensuring children build secure knowledge and encounter increasingly sophisticated learning as they progress through school.
In 2026–27, mixed-age classes follow Cycle C.
Our annual whole-school sequence is:
How Personal Development is Taught
Children receive a dedicated weekly Personal Development lesson. Teachers explicitly teach essential knowledge and vocabulary and help pupils apply their learning through discussion, stories and scenarios, practical activities, reflection and meaningful enquiry outcomes.
Reinforced through assemblies, collective worship, retrieval, class discussion and links across the wider curriculum.
Experienced through visitors, educational visits, Bikeability, RNLI learning, environmental work, charity projects, pupil leadership and community involvement.
Lived through our school vision and rules, Behaviour Curriculum, restorative conversations, routines, playtimes, relationships and expectations.
Growing & Changing
Alongside the main Health & Wellbeing curriculum, pupils in Years 4, 5 and 6 receive an age-specific Growing & Changing entitlement every year:
This ensures essential knowledge about puberty, menstruation, body changes, personal hygiene and emotional changes is introduced and revisited at an appropriate developmental stage.
In Year 6 only, pupils also receive a small amount of additional, age-appropriate non-statutory sex education covering human conception, pregnancy, foetal development and birth.
Parents may request withdrawal from these specific additional Year 6 sex education lessons. Parents cannot withdraw children from statutory Relationships Education, Health Education or National Curriculum Science.
Year 4 – Getting Ready for Puberty
Year 5 – Understanding Puberty
Inclusion & Safeguarding
Safeguarding is a golden thread throughout all six strands. Pupils learn to recognise unsafe situations and unhealthy behaviour, understand personal boundaries and privacy, identify trusted adults, communicate concerns and seek help.
Teaching is adapted appropriately for pupils with SEND while maintaining ambitious expectations and the intended curriculum entitlement.
Our curriculum also reflects the diversity of modern Britain and helps pupils develop respect for different families, identities, beliefs, cultures and experiences.
Personal Development in Sidlesham
Our rural and coastal setting is deliberately reflected in the curriculum. Children learn about road and cycling safety, beach and water safety, countryside and farm safety, environmental responsibility and how to contribute positively to their local community.
Parent & Carer Information
Parents and carers are children’s first educators and we value partnership and transparency.
Personal Development Curriculum – Parent and Carer Guide 2026–27 Relationships, Sex and Health Education (RSHE) Policy
Full Personal Development Curriculum Overview – Cycles A, B & C
Parents and carers can also request to view teaching materials or speak to the Headteacher about any aspect of the curriculum.

Governors
The Governing body for the school consists of a number of local people with differing experience but with the single aim of ensuring the school continues to prosper and improve.
Stuart Blunden Chair of Governors
Stuart Blunden
Mr Blunden and his wife have been providing child care in the local area for more than 25 years. He has held seats at the Local Authority on the Schools Forum as a Maintained Primary Governor; served two elected terms upon W.S.C.C. Children's and Young People's Services Select Committee as a Parent Governor representative; held the position of Chair of Governors at East Wittering for 14 years; Local Authority Governor at Sidlesham Primary School for 7 years and formerly a member of the Executive Committee of the West Sussex GovernorsAssociation.
Kerry Blanshard Vice Chair of Governors
Kerry Blanshard
Mrs Blanshard has worked within Children's Services for nearly 20 years, working in different local authorities around the country before selling back in West Sussex. She started her working life as a Family Support Worker and is now a Service Manager within West Sussex Children's Services. Mrs Blanshard thoroughly enjoys her role working alongside children and families and leading a team of around 40 staff who work hard to support positive outcomes for children across the Chichester district. She is a very proud Mum of two girls, one who attends secondary school and another here at Sidlesham Primary School. Mrs Blanshard loves where she lives here in Sidlesham and enjoys exploring the local area with her two labradors.
Sophia Koiston
Mrs Koiston is our headteacher. She has worked in education since 2011 and joined Sidlesham Primary School in April 2024. Prior to this, she worked as headteacher, deputy headteacher and SENCO in a variety of schools in West Sussex. Outside of school, she enjoys spending time with her husband and three children who all keep her very busy!
Jess White Co-opted Governor
Jess White
Mrs White has worked in the events and marketing industry for several years. Before embarking on family life she was a Client Director for a global events and marketing agency. A Chartered Marketer with a Master's in strategic marketing, Mrs White now works as a freelance consultant for a range of SME's supporting them with all things marketing and business development. She also co-owns a live events business with her husband, which they founded together and that he runs on a day-to-day basis. Together they have raised several hundreds of thousands of pounds for children's charities through events. A proud mother of two daughters, and a lover of the sea, if she's not exercising, or running around after the children, Mrs White can normally be found curled up reading a good book!
Cordelia Renouf Parent Governor
Cordelia Renouf
Mrs Renouf is a proud mum to two boys and a part time teacher. She trained at the university of Brighton and has been teaching for 17 years. Mrs Renouf has had experience of teaching both KS1 and KS2 as well as leading a variety of subjects across the curriculum. She grew up between London and West Wittering, where she spent many happy years mucking out stables and driving her horse around the countryside. Since becoming a wife and mother, she enjoys family life with her husband, two children and two yappy little terriers, cycling, walking and exploring the beach. In rare moments of alone time, she can usually be found baking or creating something!
Nikki Barber Co-opted Governor
Nikki Barber
Nikki Barber has worked in education for over 10 years, beginning her career as a Primary School teacher before moving into her current role with the Hampshire Inspection and Advisory Service (HIAS). She is passionate about supporting schools on their improvement journeys. As a school governor, Nikki values the opportunity to contribute to the continued development and success of Sidlesham Primary School. She has a young toddler who keeps her on her toes and loves spending time exploring the local area—whether that's enjoying the countryside or relaxing by the beach.
Caroline Harmer Clerk to Governors

Subject Overview
Intent
At Sidlesham, music is a universal language that inspires creativity, self-expression, and a sense of community.Our curriculum enables pupils to sing, play, compose, listen, and evaluate across a rich and diverse musical landscape.
It ensures that all pupils know more, remember more, and can do more as musicians — developing secure musicianship (pulse, rhythm, pitch, dynamics, tempo, timbre, structure, and texture), fluent technical skills (voice and instruments), and critical listening across historical periods, genres, styles, and traditions.
Our curriculum intent aligns with:
Our aims are to ensure that all pupils:
“Pupils should think and work like musicians – listening, performing, composing, and reflecting through sound.” (Ofsted, 2023)
Implementation
Curriculum design and sequencing
Music is taught weekly across the school through a three-year rolling programme that balances musicianship, performance, composition, and appraisal.
Each unit includes clear progression in musical concepts (pulse, rhythm, pitch, texture, structure, dynamics, tempo) and practical musicianship (voice and instrument control, notation, improvisation, ensemble skills).
Learning is sequenced from:
Knowledge builds cumulatively, enabling pupils to revisit and deepen their understanding of core ideas across phases.
EYFS – Laying the foundations
In the Early Years, children develop musical awareness through Expressive Arts and Design, Physical Development and Communication & Language. They:
By the end of EYFS, children can keep a steady beat, sing tunefully within a small range, and create and respond to patterns—providing strong foundations for KS1 musicianship.
Move rhythmically, responding to pulse and mood.
Explore instruments and create simple sound patterns.
Classroom teaching and progression
Each year group takes part in weekly classroom music, developing musicianship through:
Progression follows the Model Music Curriculum trajectory—from maintaining a pulse and simple call-and-response in KS1 to multi-part performance, notation reading, and harmony in KS2.
Enrichment and instrumental provision
Sidlesham’s music offer extends far beyond the classroom:
Whole-Class Ensemble Teaching (WCET)
Associate Music Teacher Programme
An Associate Music Teacher enhances the curriculum through:
These sessions strengthen inclusion, allow for additional progression routes, and help identify musical potential.
Performance and community engagement
Assessment
Progress is measured formatively through observation, rehearsal, and performance. Teachers assess how pupils:
End-of-unit recordings and class performances provide clear evidence of progress and are used for moderation across phases.
Use and apply musical vocabulary accurately.
Reflect and improve through rehearsal and discussion.
Impact
Through high-quality teaching, consistent participation, and rich musical experiences, pupils at Sidlesham:
Develop secure knowledge and musicianshipThey demonstrate confident control of pulse, rhythm and pitch, can read and perform simple notation, and understand how music is constructed and expressed.
Express themselves creativelyThey compose, improvise, and perform with confidence, applying knowledge of structure, dynamics and texture to communicate mood and meaning.
Appreciate music’s diversity and purposeThey experience music as both a personal and shared art form, exploring traditions from around the world and developing respect for cultural diversity.
Participate and achieveAll pupils engage meaningfully in classroom and ensemble music-making, and many choose to extend this through clubs, performances and further study.They leave Sidlesham with the knowledge, skills, and confidence to enjoy music for life.

Diary Dates

Attendance
At Sidlesham Primary School, we believe that good attendance is essential for children to succeed.
Being in school every day helps pupils to learn, build friendships and feel part of our school community.
Our Expectation
We aim for all pupils to achieve at least 96% attendance wherever possible.
We expect pupils to:
attend school every day
We know that even small amounts of absence can have a significant impact on progress.
Working Together
We take a support-first approach to attendance.
We recognise that absence is often a sign that a child or family may need support. We work closely with families to understand any barriers and provide help where needed.
Our Family Worker, Hester Johnson-Cadwell, plays a key role in supporting pupils and families with attendance and wellbeing.
//www.youtube.com/embed/iTM9mSv4ABo?si=vp-SffUMIwwlgdZl" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" referrerpolicy="strict-origin-when-cross-origin" allowfullscreen>#t=0.5" width="560" height="314" allowfullscreen="allowfullscreen" data-mce-fragment="1">
Is my child too ill for school?
Reporting Absence
If your child is unwell, please contact the school office by 9:00am on the first day of absence.
If we do not receive a reason for absence, we will contact you to ensure your child is safe.
Punctuality
The school day begins at 8:30am.
Pupils should arrive by 8:40am
The register closes at 9:10am
Arriving late can disrupt learning and may be recorded as an unauthorised absence if persistent.
How We Monitor Attendance
We monitor attendance closely and take early action where needed.
Attendance is reviewed regularly to:
identify patterns of absence
provide early support
ensure all pupils remain on track
Where attendance falls below expected levels, we will work with families to improve it.
Attendance Support
We use a graduated approach to support attendance:
96%+ – Excellent attendance
90–91% – Attendance concern
Below 90% – Persistent absence (additional support provided)
Support may include meetings, attendance plans and involvement from external services where appropriate.
Attendance and Safeguarding
Attendance is an important part of safeguarding.
We follow up all unexplained absence on the first day and may carry out additional checks if we are unable to contact families.
This ensures that all pupils are safe and supported.
Further Information
For full details, please see our Attendance Policy.
If you have any concerns about your child’s attendance, please contact the school - we are here to help.
Diary Dates

E-Safety
At Sidlesham Primary School, keeping children safe online is a key part of our safeguarding responsibility.
We teach pupils how to use technology safely, responsibly and respectfully, both in school and at home.
Our Approach
Online safety is taught through our curriculum, including computing and PSHE.
Children learn how to:
stay safe when using the internet
recognise risks and report concerns
use technology responsibly
understand how to protect their personal information
We regularly revisit these messages to ensure pupils develop secure and safe habits.
Supporting Parents
We recognise that keeping children safe online is a shared responsibility between school and home.
We encourage parents and carers to:
talk regularly with their child about their online activity
know what devices their child is using
set clear expectations around screen time and online behaviour
use parental controls where available
If you would like support or advice, please contact the school.
Top Tips for Online Safety
Keep devices in shared family spaces where possible
Set clear rules about when and how devices can be used
Check age restrictions on apps, games and social media
Encourage your child to speak to you if something worries them
Remind children never to share personal information online
​Gaming and Devices
Many devices and apps include parental controls which can help you manage what your child can access.
setting up child accounts with correct age information
enabling parental controls on devices and apps
regularly reviewing settings as your child grows
This helps ensure children are using technology in a safe and age-appropriate way.
Reporting Concerns
If you or your child are concerned about something that has happened online, it is important to act quickly.
report concerns to CEOP (Child Exploitation and Online Protection)
https://www.ceop.police.uk
All concerns will be taken seriously and handled sensitively.
​Useful links
Thinkuknow (CEOP) – advice and activities for children and parents
NSPCC Online Safety – guidance for families
UK Safer Internet Centre – resources and support
These websites provide practical advice to help keep children safe online.

The School Day
At Sidlesham Primary School, we have clear routines that help children feel settled, safe and ready to learn.
Our school day is carefully structured to ensure pupils make the most of their learning time while also enjoying opportunities to play, socialise and relax.
Start of the Day
School doors open at 8:30am
Pupils should arrive by 8:40am
The school day begins promptly at 8:40am
Children enter school independently, helping them to develop confidence and responsibility.
Morning work is ready for pupils on arrival so that learning begins straight away.
Daily Routine
A typical day includes:
Assembly: 9:30am – 9:45am
Morning break: 10:45am – 11:00am
Lunch: 12:00pm – 1:00pm
Afternoon learning: 1:00pm onwards
Our structured day supports a calm and purposeful learning environment.
Late Arrival
If your child arrives after 8:40am, they must be brought to the school office and signed in.
Registers close at 9:10am, after which arrival may be recorded as an unauthorised absence in line with national guidance.
End of the Day
The school day ends at 3:10pm.
Teachers supervise pupils as they leave the building to ensure a safe and smooth end to the day.
If your child is being collected by someone different, please inform the school office in advance.
Safeguarding
For safeguarding reasons:
visitors must report to the school office and sign in
children should enter school independently unless prior arrangements are made
These procedures help us to keep all pupils safe.
Total School Hours
The school week totals 32.5 hours, in line with Department for Education expectations.
Diary Dates

Uniform
At Sidlesham Primary School, our uniform helps to create a sense of belonging, pride and readiness for learning.
We aim to keep our uniform simple, practical and affordable for all families.
Our Approach
Our uniform is designed to:
promote equality between pupils
be practical and safe for school activities

Navy shorts (logo optional)
Trainers or plimsolls
Navy jogging bottoms

SEND
At Sidlesham Primary School, we are committed to ensuring that every child is supported to succeed.
We are an inclusive school where pupils with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) are fully valued and supported to achieve their potential. Our approach reflects our values of Ambition, Confidence and Kindness.
Our Approach
We believe that high-quality teaching is the first step in supporting all pupils.
adapt teaching to meet the needs of all learners
provide additional support where needed
work closely with families and external professionals
ensure pupils feel confident, included and supported
We recognise that every child is different and tailor our provision accordingly.
How We Support Our Pupils
Support may include:
adapted classroom teaching and resources
small group or one-to-one support
targeted interventions
support for social, emotional and mental health
external agency involvement where appropriate
We regularly review progress to ensure support is effective and responsive to pupils’ needs.
